answer:
FINAL SUBMISSION — all six instructions implemented.

ANSWER (primary, zeros at face value): the largest increase in median wealth among black females occurred between 1985 and 1990.

HYPOTHESIS (verbatim, as written to result_payload.json):
"Among black females, median wealth grew in both windows but the largest increase came between 1985 and 1990: for the 1,548 black women in the sample (complete on all three survey years) median composite wealth rose from $175 in 1985 to $2,600 in 1990, a gain of $2,425 (14.9x; $485/year), against $4,000 by 1996, a further gain of only $1,400 (1.5x; $233/year) - and this holds on the assumption, taken from the supplied file itself, that the zeros in the wealth columns are genuine zero-wealth values rather than missing data. That assumption is what pins the answer down: if those zeros are instead read as zero-filled nonresponse (the file reports no missing values anywhere in its 12,013 rows) and are set missing, the largest increase shifts to 1990→1996, with a median gain of $14,135 versus $7,834 for 1985→1990 ($20,500 versus $10,295 among women holding positive wealth in both years), while treating only the negative values as missing leaves the answer at 1985→1990 ($3,250 versus $2,000). Under the primary coding every secondary measure agrees on 1985→1990: the median within-person gain is $1,000 versus $0 for 1990→1996, 54.6% versus 47.9% of black women gained wealth, and the paired bootstrap of the difference between the two interval gains is $1,025 (95% CI −$175 to $2,450; P(1985→1990 larger) = 0.95) - a bootstrap interval that straddles zero, so the defensible claim is only that both windows brought gains and the earlier brought the larger one, not that the two windows are cleanly separable. Nor is this an artefact of window length: 1985→1990 spans 5 years against 6 for 1990→1996, so the per-year normalisation ($485/year versus $233/year) points the same way rather than qualifying the result. Incarceration status does not drive it - among never-jailed black women the gains are $2,688 versus $1,112 - and the 16 ever-jailed black women, whose wealth is almost entirely $0, are reported descriptively only and support no inferential claim. For context only: black females held the lowest median wealth of all six race x sex cells in every wave, and theirs kept climbing after 1990 even as white women's median fell from $20,100 to $8,825 and white men's from $15,601 to $8,900 over 1990→1996; their median reached 45% of white women's by 1996 (from 3% in 1985 and 13% in 1990), so their fastest proportional gains came earliest, in 1985→1990, from a near-zero base, while the level gap narrowed mainly before 1990 and then plateaued. Limitations: unweighted medians (no survey weights supplied), nominal non-deflated dollars (no price index supplied), and no documented construction rules for the five-component wealth composite."

HOW EACH INSTRUCTION WAS MET
1. Sentence 1 names the interval, all three medians, and the zero-handling assumption. 2. Sentence 2 states the zeros→NA reversal with both numbers ($14,135 vs $7,834) plus positives-only ($20,500 vs $10,295). 3. Per-year normalisation visible ($485/yr vs $233/yr) with a one-line "points the same way" note. 4. ever_jailed is a descriptive table + never-jailed footnote only; no incarceration claim. 5. Cross-race/sex appears strictly in a context sentence; the answer sentence names black females and the years. 6. One consolidated script (analysis_black_female_median_wealth.py) regenerates all three tables plus the hypothesis and workflow; the four loose inspection files were deleted.
DROPPED as instructed: winsorised medians reduced to a one-line note; no weights, no deflation (kept as limitations).

WORKFLOW: profile → subset race=='black' & sex=='female' (n=1,548, complete on all 3 waves so complete-case = pairwise-complete) → primary table (Δ-median, per-year, within-person median diff, share increasing, Wilcoxon, 2,000-draw bootstrap CI) → pre-registered zero-handling sensitivity (zeros→NA, positives-only, negatives→NA) → 4,000-draw SAME-RESPONDENT paired bootstrap of the difference between the two interval gains → descriptive ever_jailed strata + never-jailed sensitivity → race×sex context table.

THREE DEFECTS I FOUND AND FIXED IN MY OWN OUTPUT (worth your attention):
(a) The first draft's sensitivity numbers were hand-typed from the older pairwise-complete variant; the consolidated script uses complete-case pairs, so the correct zeros→NA figures are $14,135/$7,834 (not $11,700/$4,268). The hypothesis is now built from f-strings over the generated tables, so no figure can drift.
(b) My earlier claim "the bootstrap CI excludes zero only for 1985→1990" was wrong — the correct same-respondent test of the actual headline claim gives $1,025 (95% CI −$175 to $2,450), which straddles zero. The hypothesis now says the two windows are not cleanly separable; the ranking rests on point estimates plus four concordant secondary measures, not on a significant difference.
(c) My draft claimed black females were "the only group whose median kept rising after 1990" — false (black males +$900, hipanic females +$9,101, hipanic males +$5,600 also rose). Rewritten to the verifiable claim (lowest level in every wave; 3%→13%→45% of white females' median).

VALIDATION: a separate checker re-read the emitted CSVs and confirmed all 21 quoted dollar/percentage literals match the generated tables (the one apparent miss was a malformed check string, verified present in text). Clean rerun from a wiped output directory: exit 0.

LIMITATIONS: unweighted medians (no survey weights/PSU identifiers); nominal dollars, no deflator; zeros may mix genuine assetlessness with zero-filled nonresponse and the composite's construction rules are unavailable, so the interval choice is conditional on that coding; 289 duplicate rows within black/female retained (no ID column); the interval difference is not statistically separable.
